To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

secondary-structure features can be used to improve splice-site prediction and that the secondary-structure features are biologically relevant and capture known splice-site regulatory signals such as splicesilencers.

(1) RNA secondary-structure features are important in splice-site recognition; (2) the secondary-structure features can be generated using our feature generation approach; (3) the splice-site model employing both the sequence and structure features is significantly more accurate than the sequence-based splice-site model; (4) the secondary-structures around the splice-site are important for splice-site recognition; and (5) the secondary-structural features can capture biologically relevant information.
